increments.outcome: Explain an inherited decision from a restorable archive
Use recovered reasoning in a meeting

stories.title: Open the right door
stories.statement: As an administrator, I want organizational and project policies to grant Collect or Consult access, so authorized people can use the appropriate employee knowledge.
stories.scope: LDAP supplies current identities, groups, and available organizational attributes. The shared UI applies subtree, project, and evidence policies and explains an individual access decision.

stories.title: Ask Alex why from the email record
stories.statement: As a successor, I want to ask about a decision preserved in approved email, so I can recover its documented rationale.
stories.scope: one declared email import format including attachment capture, one employee, question and answer, and source passage access.

stories.title: Bring the design document into the explanation
stories.statement: As a successor, I want design files considered alongside email, so I can recover constraints documented elsewhere.
stories.scope: one declared file format; no OCR or universal document browser.

stories.title: Recover what was said in the meeting
stories.statement: As a successor, I want meeting evidence attributed to its speakers, so I can distinguish recommendations, disagreement, and adopted decisions.
stories.scope: one speaker-labeled transcript format; no transcription service.

stories.title: Seal it and bring it back
stories.statement: As a custodian, I want the employee archive restored from the encrypted Mortuary, so consultation survives loss of the intake session and departed account.
stories.scope: publish and restore one identifiable casket revision; no storage console.

stories.title: Ask from the time it happened
stories.statement: As a successor, I want a historical cutoff, so I can understand the employee’s documented perspective without hindsight.
stories.scope: an as-of date, a retrospective mode, and fresh context when switching.

stories.title: Follow the decision as it changes
stories.statement: As a successor, I want to follow and compare a decision’s stages, so I can understand what changed, why it changed, and which reasoning persisted.
stories.scope: one decision trail with a two-date comparison. A chronological list or table is enough.

stories.title: Recover the missing chapter
stories.statement: As a custodian, I want to add missed evidence to a new casket revision, so explanations improve while earlier sessions retain an identifiable evidence basis.
stories.scope: retrieve, add or reprocess selected material, and republish; one updater.

stories.title: Bring Alex into the room
stories.statement: As a host, I want a topic meeting with a fixed human roster and an employee representation, so colleagues can investigate the record together.
stories.scope: text, one representation, fixed participants, pinned revision and perspective.

stories.title: Give the virtual colleague a seat
stories.statement: As a host, I want a separately authorized virtual employee to participate, so it can contribute questions within its permitted scope.
stories.scope: one configured virtual identity; no delegation chains or external actions.

stories.title: Test yesterday’s reasoning against today’s problem
stories.statement: As a participant, I want to supply a current requirement, so I can identify which historical assumptions still matter.
stories.scope: attributed scenario facts and generated advice; no autonomous execution.

stories.title: Leave with the decision trail
stories.statement: As a host, I want a saved brief and transcript, so the recovered understanding remains useful after the meeting.
stories.scope: What we learned, How the decision evolved, What remains uncertain, and Next check.
